cards.text: In those days, Caesar Augustus, the Roman emperor, sends out a decree to take a census of the whole empire. It's the first census while Quirinius is governor of Syria. Friend, I spent years under a pile of warranty cards nobody ever mailed in, and even I think that's a LOT of paperwork.

cards.question: Caesar wants the whole empire counted. Where does each person go to register?

cards.text: So Joseph, a man living in Nazareth in Galilee, heads up to Judea, to the city of David called Bethlehem. No car, no bus, no snack stops. Just Joseph and the road.

cards.question: Joseph has to register in Bethlehem because he's from the house and line of ___.

cards.text: And he's not going alone. Mary, who's pledged to marry him, goes to register too, and she's expecting a child. A trip to Judea with a baby on the way, all for government paperwork? I can't even get through a dusty instruction manual without a nap.

cards.question: Mary's baby is born after she and Joseph get back home to Nazareth.

cards.text: Mary gives birth to her firstborn, a Son, and wraps Him in swaddling cloths. Now she needs somewhere to lay Him down.

cards.question: Mary has just wrapped her newborn Son in swaddling cloths. Where does she lay Him?
Mary lays her newborn Son in a manger. Why there?

answers.text: No room for them in the inn

cards.text: Meanwhile, shepherds in the fields nearby are working the night shift, keeping watch over their flocks. And everybody knows nothing EVER happens on the night shift.

cards.question: Shepherds are out in the fields at night. Just then, who stands right in front of them?
An angel of the Lord stands before the shepherds, and the glory of the Lord shines around them. The shepherds are ___.

cards.text: Then the angel speaks: "Do not be afraid!" Friend, that's a LOT to ask of a guy who just watched the dark light up with the glory of the Lord.

cards.question: The angel says his good news of great joy is only for the shepherds.

cards.text: Then comes the big news: "Today in the city of David a Savior has been born to you."

cards.question: The angel tells the shepherds who this newborn Savior is. What does he call Him?

answers.text: A prophet of the Most High

cards.question: The angel gives the shepherds a sign: they'll find a baby wrapped in swaddling cloths and lying in a ___.

cards.text: Suddenly a great multitude of the heavenly host appears with the angel, praising God. They say, "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men on whom His favor rests!"
Then the angels leave them and go into heaven. And it's just the shepherds and the sheep again, standing in the dark, blinking.

cards.question: The angels are gone. What do the shepherds say to one another?

answers.text: Let's go to Bethlehem and see
Let's ask the town elders first

cards.question: The shepherds take their time getting to Bethlehem.

cards.text: They find Mary and Joseph, and the Baby lying in the manger. No address, no map, just a baby in a manger, and they FOUND Him!

cards.question: After seeing the Child, the shepherds keep the message they received about Him to themselves.
The shepherds tell people about the Child. All who hear what the shepherds say are ___.

cards.text: Everybody's amazed and talking. But Mary? Mary's got a different reaction.

cards.question: Everyone's talking about what the shepherds said. What does Mary do with all these things?

answers.text: Treasures them up and ponders them

cards.question: The shepherds head back to their fields. How do they go?
Everything the shepherds heard and saw was just as the angel had told them.

cards.text: That's where we'll leave it for now, friend. But this story's still got a few pages left in it.

findings.problem: "Just Joseph and the road" says Joseph travels alone. Luke 2:5 says he went there with Mary, so the card states something the text shows is wrong. Card 5 then reverses it.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 3 says "the city of David called Bethlehem" right before this blank asks "the house and line of ___" with David as the answer. The setup puts the answer word on screen and rules out Aaron and Saul.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has 4 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't share the fact's core action. The fact is making a long trip while expecting a child, just to register. The comparison is staying awake through an instruction manual. One is travel and the other is tedium, so the comparison doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card tells the amazement from Luke 2:18 ("Everybody's amazed") but cites only Luke 2:19. The citation should be Luke 2:18-19.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "Everybody's amazed and talking" adds talking. Luke 2:18 says only that all who heard were amazed.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "Everyone's talking about what the shepherds said" adds talking. Luke 2:18 says the hearers were amazed.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
